paper_title: EvoMoE Expert Evolution in Mixture of Experts for Multimodal Large   Language Models
caption: : EvoMoE

model_annotations.Bulgarian: The diagram presents two side-by-side bar charts, labeled "Text" and "Image", which illustrate the distribution of percentages across different "MoE layer idx" categories for four distinct "Expert" categories. The horizontal axis represents the "MoE layer idx" and is labeled with numerical values ranging from 1 to 23 in increments of 2, while the vertical axis represents the "Percentage" and is labeled with values from 0% to 100% in increments of 25%. Each chart contains a series of grouped bars, with four bars per group corresponding to "Expert 1" through "Expert 4", colored blue, orange, green, and red, respectively. In the "Text" chart, the bars for "Expert 1" start at around 80% and decrease in height as "MoE layer idx" increases, while "Expert 2", "Expert 3", and "Expert 4" start at lower percentages and generally increase. In the "Image" chart, "Expert 1" starts at a very low percentage and increases, while "Expert 4" remains consistently high across all "MoE layer idx" values. The bars are organized in groups according to their "MoE layer idx" values, and the height of each bar corresponds to its respective percentage value. The charts do not display any specific sorting or highlighting of particular bars.
model_annotations.German: The diagram presents a comparison of the percentage distribution of four experts across different MoE (Mixture of Experts) layers for both text and image data. The horizontal axis represents the MoE layer index, ranging from 1 to 23, while the vertical axis represents the percentage, ranging from 0% to 100%. The bars are grouped by data type (text and image) and are further divided into four categories representing the four experts, labeled as Expert 1 to Expert 4 and distinguished by different colors. For the text data, Expert 1 starts at around 85% for layer index 1 and decreases to approximately 20% for subsequent layers, while Expert 2 starts at around 15% and remains relatively consistent. Experts 3 and 4 are mostly around 0% for initial layers but gain prominence in later layers, with Expert 3 and Expert 4 showing significant presence from layer 5 onwards. For the image data, Expert 1 starts at around 15% and increases to 100% for later layers, while Expert 2 is consistently at 0%. Expert 3 is prominent in initial layers but decreases, whereas Expert 4 is mostly around 0% but gains some presence in certain layers. The bars are not explicitly sorted in a particular order, and no specific bars are visually highlighted.
